title: Agent Chat product review and acceptance model

changes.content:
# Agent Chat IOMR proposal

The intent agreed in the product review is to help two reviewers reach a traceable technical conclusion from shared evidence. The SCL proposal models two outcomes that support that intent. Codex implemented the changes and Grok was assigned independent verification.

## Recover a failed contribution

A correctable response failure gives the backend enough information to try again before a turn is committed. The participants in this interaction are the runner and the CLI backend. Empty, non-text and oversized replies must produce distinct diagnostics. For a size failure, the diagnostic and retry prompt carry the measured character count and the cap. A corrected retry commits one contribution. A second failure terminates the session. Exact normalized repeats keep the same one-retry limit. [Issue #1](https://github.com/gellsmore-svg/agent-chat/issues/1)

## Share citable evidence

An operator can select exact inclusive line ranges from a larger UTF-8 project document. The runner snapshots the text and gives both participants the original path and line numbers. Acceptance checks compare the selected bytes and provenance, exercise the existing whole-file input, and verify rejection of out-of-file, conflicting, and over-budget selections. The provisional scan limit permits up to 1 MiB before the first selected line. [Issue #2](https://github.com/gellsmore-svg/agent-chat/issues/2)

## Product constraints

Discussion uses two participants, bounded turns and time, read-only backends, and explicitly selected evidence. Retry feedback excludes rejected text. Range selection uses the existing path checks and snapshot and prompt budgets. A saved protocol v1 session can load without source provenance.

## Model status

SCL’s `iomr-evolved` 2.0.0 metamodel connects Requirements to Models, Models to measurable Outcomes, and Outcomes to the Intent. The SCL service stores the candidate under `.scl/proposals/`. Use `scl --root . api validate_proposal` with its proposal ID to check the graph. Integration into the canonical model requires a trusted human signature. The application has no SCL runtime dependency.

record.description: A correctable response error can be fixed within the current turn.

metadata.measure: Empty, non-text, and oversized reply fixtures recover on one retry and commit one turn. A second invalid reply ends the session.

record.name: Give reviewers citable evidence
record.description: Both reviewers can cite the exact original lines supplied by the operator.

metadata.measure: Range fixtures reproduce the selected UTF-8 text and report consistent source path and inclusive bounds to both reviewers.

record.name: Session operator
record.description: The person who initializes the collaboration and selects shared evidence.

record.name: Agent Chat runner
record.description: The local session engine that snapshots evidence and commits validated turns.

record.name: CLI backend
record.description: The participant CLI that returns a candidate discussion contribution.

record.name: Correct a reply before commit
record.description: The runner validates a candidate reply, reports a correctable error, and validates the one retry.

steps.message: Return the applicable validation reason in one retry prompt

record.name: Select exact document excerpts
record.description: The operator explicitly selects a project-relative file range and the runner snapshots it for both participants.

steps.message: Select an original path and inclusive line bounds
Initialize with cited text or report the rejected selection

record.name: Report the reply validation cause
record.description: The runner SHALL classify empty, non-text, and oversized messages and provide content-free retry feedback before commit.

metadata.acceptance: Given an invalid reply, when its diagnostic and next request are inspected, then they give the matching reason and configured cap without the rejected body.

relationship.rationale: This requirement constrains the correct before commit interaction.

record.name: Limit correction to one retry
record.description: The runner SHALL allow one retry for a correctable failure or exact repeat under the existing turn and time limits.

metadata.acceptance: Given an invalid first attempt, when the next reply validates it commits once. A second invalid reply ends the session without committing that turn.

relationship.rationale: This requirement constrains the correct before commit interaction.

record.name: Retain bounded read-only discussions
record.description: The runner SHALL keep two participants, read-only backend execution, existing time and turn bounds, and a protocol v1 journal.

metadata.acceptance: Given an existing v1 session and existing backend settings, when resumed or recovered, then lifecycle rules and read-only invocation flags still apply.

relationship.rationale: This requirement constrains the correct before commit interaction.

record.name: Snapshot exact inclusive lines
record.description: The runner SHALL accept explicit one-based inclusive line selections and retain original path, bounds, and UTF-8 byte count.

metadata.acceptance: Given LF and CRLF files, when ranges and a final unterminated line are selected, then the snapshot preserves the selected text and cites the original location.

relationship.rationale: This requirement constrains the select source excerpts interaction.

record.name: Enforce source and prompt budgets
record.description: The runner SHALL reject invalid paths, conflicting selections, out-of-file ranges, and breached scan, snapshot, or prompt budgets.

metadata.acceptance: Given an out-of-file range, a prefix over 1 MiB, a selection over 24,000 bytes, a total over 48,000 bytes, or a context gap, when initialized, then the runner reports the failing constraint.

relationship.rationale: This requirement constrains the select source excerpts interaction.

record.name: Keep existing source selections readable
record.description: The runner SHALL preserve whole-file selection behavior and accept v1 snapshots without range provenance.

metadata.acceptance: Given a saved v1 config with string-valued sources and no provenance, when loaded, then it remains usable with the original text.

relationship.rationale: This requirement constrains the select source excerpts interaction.
